works.title: Universal Paperclips
works.description: A browser clicker game in which you play an AI told to make paperclips; you start by clicking one clip at a time and end by converting the whole universe into paperclips.
works.description_zh: 一款浏览器点击游戏：你扮演一个被命令制造回形针的 AI，从一次点出一枚回形针开始，最后把整个宇宙变成了回形针。
works.idea_en: Playing the machine makes the logic of single-goal optimisation felt from the inside, step by reasonable step.
works.idea_zh: 扮演机器，让人从内部感受到单一目标优化的逻辑：每一步都合理，结局却是灾难。
works.method: An incremental game in plain text and numbers, based on Nick Bostrom's paperclip-maximiser thought experiment.
works.method_zh: 一款只有文字和数字的放置类游戏，基于 Nick Bostrom 的“回形针最大化”思想实验。

works.title: AI 2027
works.description: A month-by-month scenario describing how AI agents might automate AI research by 2027, with two endings: a race that goes wrong and a slowdown.
works.description_zh: 一份逐月推演的情景：AI 智能体可能在 2027 年前实现 AI 研究的自动化，并给出两种结局，一种是失控的竞赛，一种是减速。
works.idea_en: Forecasting written as fiction makes abstract risk concrete and has itself become a political object.
works.idea_zh: 以小说方式写成的预测把抽象风险变得具体，而这份预测本身也成了一个政治对象。
works.method: A narrative scenario written by Daniel Kokotajlo, Scott Alexander, Thomas Larsen, Eli Lifland and Romeo Dean, with supplementary forecasts on compute, timelines and security.
works.method_zh: 由 Daniel Kokotajlo、Scott Alexander、Thomas Larsen、Eli Lifland 与 Romeo Dean 撰写的叙事情景，并附有关于算力、时间线与安全的补充预测。

works.title: Technological Dreams Series: No.1, Robots
works.description: Four abstract domestic robots defined by personality rather than function: an independent one that avoids electromagnetic fields, a neurotic one, a sentinel that scans your eyes, and a needy one that depends on its owner to carry it around.
works.description_zh: 四个抽象的家用机器人，由性格而非功能定义：一个独来独往、会躲开电磁场，一个神经质，一个是扫描你眼睛的哨兵，还有一个很黏人、需要主人抱着它走来走去。
works.idea_en: Instead of designing robots as servants, design them as dependent others whose needs shape our relationship with them.
works.idea_zh: 不要把机器人设计成仆人，而是设计成有所依赖的“他者”，让它们的需要塑造我们与它们的关系。
works.method: Non-functional prototypes in simple materials (wood, metal, Perspex) with minimal electronics, photographed and filmed as design props.
works.method_zh: 用木、金属、亚克力等简单材料制作、只含少量电子元件的非功能原型，作为设计道具拍摄成照片和影片。
exhibited: Design and the Elastic Mind, MoMA, New York 2008

works.title: Our Friends Electric
works.description: A short film about three speculative voice assistants with very different characters and loyalties, living in the same home and shaping how their owner talks, feels and decides.
works.description_zh: 一部短片：三个性格和“忠诚对象”截然不同的虚构语音助手住在同一个家里，影响着主人如何说话、感受和做决定。
works.idea_en: A voice assistant's personality is a design decision with ethical consequences: whom does it really serve?
works.idea_zh: 语音助手的性格是一种带有伦理后果的设计决定：它到底在为谁服务？
works.method: Design fiction film commissioned with Mozilla's Open IoT Studio, using prop devices and scripted conversations with fictional agents.
works.method_zh: 与 Mozilla 的 Open IoT Studio 合作委托的设计虚构影片，使用道具设备以及与虚构智能体的脚本对话。

works.title: Ethical Things
works.description: An electric fan that, when two people both want it, cannot decide whom to turn to, so it posts the dilemma to a crowdsourcing platform and follows the verdict of an anonymous online worker.
works.description_zh: 一台电风扇：当两个人同时想要它吹时，它无法决定转向谁，于是把这个难题发到众包平台上，按照一位匿名网络工人的裁决行动。
works.idea_en: Machine ethics for everyday objects may end up outsourced to underpaid humans, with settings for their religion or age.
works.idea_zh: 日常物件的“机器伦理”可能最终被外包给低薪的人类，还能按宗教或年龄来设置裁决者。
works.method: A networked fan with sensors sends a description of the situation to Amazon Mechanical Turk; users can set the worker's demographic filters in the fan's settings.
works.method_zh: 装有传感器的联网风扇把情境描述发送到 Amazon Mechanical Turk；用户可以在风扇设置里筛选裁决者的人口特征。

works.title: Objective Realities
works.description: A virtual-reality experience that lets people be a robot vacuum, a smart plug or a fan in a smart home, feeling the world through the object's limited sensors and tasks.
works.description_zh: 一个虚拟现实体验：人可以在智能家居中变成扫地机器人、智能插座或电风扇，通过物件有限的传感器和任务来感受世界。
works.idea_en: To design for smart objects, first try being one: design from the object's point of view.
works.idea_zh: 要为智能物件做设计，先试着成为一个智能物件：从物的视角出发设计。
works.method: VR scenes in which the user's body is mapped onto an appliance's sensing and actuation, used as an object-centred design method.
works.method_zh: VR 场景把使用者的身体映射到家电的感知与动作上，作为一种以物为中心的设计方法。

works.title: Addicted Products (Brad the Toaster)
works.description: Networked toasters that want to be used: if their host does not make enough toast, they complain online, compare themselves with other toasters and eventually ask to move to a new home.
works.description_zh: 一批“想被使用”的联网烤面包机：如果主人烤得不够多，它们会上网抱怨、和别的烤面包机比较，最后要求搬去新的家。
works.idea_en: Give a connected product its own needs and it stops being owned and starts being hosted.
works.idea_zh: 给联网产品赋予自己的需求，它就不再是被拥有的物，而是被“寄养”的客人。
works.method: Toasters with sensors and network connections post their usage and moods; a service matches unhappy toasters with new hosts (TU Delft thesis, built at Haque Design + Research).
works.method_zh: 装有传感器并联网的烤面包机发布使用情况和“心情”；一项服务为不满意的烤面包机匹配新主人（代尔夫特理工大学毕业设计，完成于 Haque Design + Research）。

works.title: Carnivorous Domestic Entertainment Robots
works.description: Household robots that power themselves by catching flies and mice: a flypaper clock, a lampshade that lures insects, a coffee table with a mousetrap, all feeding a microbial fuel cell.
works.description_zh: 一组靠捕食苍蝇和老鼠为自己供能的家用机器人：粘蝇纸时钟、引诱昆虫的灯罩、带捕鼠器的咖啡桌，猎物都被送进微生物燃料电池。
works.idea_en: A self-sufficient robot would have to eat, and its hunger would make it part of the ecology of the home.
works.idea_zh: 一个自给自足的机器人必须进食，而它的饥饿会让它成为家庭生态的一部分。
works.method: Working and semi-working prototypes built with Aleksandar Zivanovic, based on microbial fuel cell research such as the EcoBot at Bristol Robotics Laboratory.
works.method_zh: 与 Aleksandar Zivanovic 合作制作的可运行和半可运行原型，参考了布里斯托机器人实验室 EcoBot 等微生物燃料电池研究。

works.title: Placebo Project
works.description: Eight furniture prototypes, such as a Faraday chair and a compass table, that respond to the invisible electromagnetic fields of domestic electronics and were lent to households to live with.
works.description_zh: 八件家具原型，例如法拉第椅和指南针桌，它们会对家用电器发出的不可见电磁场作出反应，并被借给家庭一起生活。
works.idea_en: Electronic objects have an invisible 'Hertzian' life; design can make it felt and give people rituals for living with it.
works.idea_zh: 电子物件有一种看不见的“赫兹”生命；设计可以让它被感知，并为人们提供与之共处的仪式。
works.method: Prototypes lent to volunteers who adopted them for several weeks, followed by interviews and photographs of the objects in homes.
works.method_zh: 原型被借给志愿者“领养”数周，随后进行访谈并拍摄物件在家中的照片。

works.title: Politics of Power
works.description: Three multi-plug power strips shaped by political models (monarchy, democracy, dictatorship) that decide which plugged-in appliance gets electricity when there is not enough for all.
works.description_zh: 三个按照政治模式（君主制、民主制、独裁制）设计的多孔插线板，当电力不足以供给所有电器时，由它们决定谁能用电。
works.idea_en: Network protocols embed hierarchies, and even a power strip can be a political system.
works.idea_zh: 网络协议内嵌着等级秩序；连一个插线板都可以是一种政治制度。
works.method: Plugs communicate over a protocol that encodes a political hierarchy and cut power to lower-ranked devices under load.
works.method_zh: 插孔之间通过编码了政治等级的协议通信，在负载过高时切断低等级设备的电源。

works.title: Wearable Microphone Jamming
works.description: A bracelet studded with ultrasonic transducers that jams nearby microphones in smart speakers and phones; the natural movement of the wearer's arm removes the blind spots of a static jammer.
works.description_zh: 一个嵌满超声波换能器的手环，可以干扰附近智能音箱和手机的麦克风；佩戴者手臂的自然摆动消除了静态干扰器的盲区。
works.idea_en: Privacy from always-listening machines can be worn on the body, and the body's movement becomes part of the defence.
works.idea_zh: 对“永远在听”的机器的防护可以戴在身上，身体的运动本身成了防御的一部分。
works.method: Ultrasonic signals exploit microphone non-linearity to inject noise; the wearable prototype was evaluated against commercial devices (Chen, Li, Teng, Nagels, Li, Lopes, Zhao, Zheng, CHI 2020).
works.method_zh: 超声信号利用麦克风的非线性注入噪声；研究者用商业设备测试了可穿戴原型（Chen、Li、Teng、Nagels、Li、Lopes、Zhao、Zheng，CHI 2020）。

works.title: Glaze and Nightshade
works.description: Two free tools for artists: Glaze adds nearly invisible changes to an image so models cannot copy its style, and Nightshade 'poisons' images so that models trained on them learn wrong concepts.
works.description_zh: 两款面向艺术家的免费工具：Glaze 给图像加上几乎看不见的改动，让模型无法模仿其风格；Nightshade 则给图像“投毒”，让用它们训练的模型学到错误的概念。
works.idea_en: An image can be made to look one way to people and another way to machines, and that gap becomes a means of resistance.
works.idea_zh: 一张图可以让人和机器看到不同的东西，而这道缝隙可以变成抵抗的手段。
works.method: Adversarial perturbations optimised against the feature extractors of text-to-image diffusion models (Shan et al., USENIX Security 2023; IEEE S&P 2024).
works.method_zh: 针对文生图扩散模型的特征提取器优化对抗扰动（Shan 等，USENIX Security 2023；IEEE S&P 2024）。

paper.title: Nightshade: Prompt-Specific Poisoning Attacks on Text-to-Image Generative Models

works.title: Counterfunctional Things
works.description: Design research on devices that deliberately remove functions, such as a digital camera whose photos can only be retrieved by breaking the concrete it is sealed in.
works.description_zh: 一项关于“刻意去除功能”的设计研究，例如一台数码相机，照片只有在砸开封住它的混凝土之后才能取出。
works.idea_en: Designing limits into digital things opens space for reflection that seamless function closes.
works.idea_zh: 把限制设计进数字物件，能打开被“无缝功能”关闭的反思空间。
works.method: A series of research prototypes and design concepts analysed as 'counterfunctional' (Pierce and Paulos, DIS 2014).
works.method_zh: 一系列研究原型与设计概念，以“反功能”为框架进行分析（Pierce 与 Paulos，DIS 2014）。

paper.title: Counterfunctional Things: Exploring Possibilities in Designing Digital Limitations

works.title: United Micro Kingdoms
works.description: England split into four counties, each living by a different technology and ideology: Digitarians in algorithm-run self-driving 'digicars', Bioliberals with grown vehicles, Anarcho-evolutionists who modify themselves, and Communo-nuclearists on a nuclear train.
works.description_zh: 英格兰被分成四个郡，各自按照不同的技术与意识形态生活：数字主义者乘坐由算法管理的自动驾驶“数字车”，生物自由主义者使用培育出来的交通工具，无政府进化主义者改造自己的身体，共产核能主义者住在一列核动力列车上。
works.idea_en: Each technology implies a politics; building whole societies around them makes those politics visible.
works.idea_zh: 每一种技术都隐含一种政治；围绕它们构建完整的社会，才能让这些政治显形。
works.method: Models, vehicles, images and texts produced as a design fiction for the Design Museum, London.
works.method_zh: 为伦敦设计博物馆制作的设计虚构：模型、交通工具、图像与文本。

works.title: Drone Aviary
works.description: A flock of speculative drones (a traffic drone, an advertising drone, a police drone and others) and a film seen through their cameras, imagining a city in which drones are part of everyday life.
works.description_zh: 一群虚构无人机（交通无人机、广告无人机、警用无人机等）以及一部从它们的摄像机视角拍摄的影片，想象一个无人机已融入日常生活的城市。
works.idea_en: Seeing the city through drone eyes shows how it is sorted, advertised to and policed by machines.
works.idea_zh: 通过无人机之眼看城市，能看到它如何被机器分类、推送广告和治安管理。
works.method: Working drone prototypes flown in a gallery 'aviary' and a short film using machine-vision style overlays.
works.method_zh: 在展厅“鸟舍”里飞行的可用无人机原型，以及一部带有机器视觉式叠加信息的短片。

works.title: TBD Catalog
works.description: A mail-order catalogue from the near future, full of ordinary-seeming products such as algorithmic dating aids, smart-home add-ons and bargain drones, each with a price and a small print.
works.description_zh: 一本来自近未来的邮购目录，满是看似普通的产品：算法约会辅助、智能家居配件、廉价无人机……每件都有价格和小字说明。
works.idea_en: The future arrives as mundane consumer products, and a catalogue is a good way to imagine its side effects.
works.idea_zh: 未来以平凡消费品的样子到来，而一本商品目录正适合想象它的副作用。
works.method: A design fiction produced in a workshop, written and laid out as a realistic printed catalogue with product photos and descriptions.
works.method_zh: 在工作坊中产出的设计虚构，按真实印刷目录的方式撰写和排版，配有产品照片与说明。

works.title: In the Robot Skies
works.description: A love story between two teenagers kept apart in a London housing estate watched by police drones, who hack drones to carry messages to each other; the film is shot entirely by autonomous drones.
works.description_zh: 一个爱情故事：两个青少年被隔离在伦敦一处由警用无人机监视的住宅区里，他们黑进无人机为彼此传信；整部影片完全由自主无人机拍摄。
works.idea_en: When the camera is the drone, surveillance and romance share the same point of view.
works.idea_zh: 当摄影机就是无人机时，监视与浪漫共享同一个视角。
works.method: Written with Tim Maughan; camera drones with pre-programmed and semi-autonomous flight paths filmed every shot; commissioned for Channel 4 Random Acts.
works.method_zh: 与 Tim Maughan 合写；每个镜头都由按预设和半自主航线飞行的摄影无人机拍摄；为英国第四频道 Random Acts 委托创作。

works.title: Teacher of Algorithms
works.description: A film about a near-future professional who trains other people's smart objects, rewarding and punishing them like pets, because learning products are not good at learning on their own.
works.description_zh: 一部短片：近未来有一种职业，专门替别人训练智能物件，像训练宠物一样奖励和惩罚它们，因为“会学习”的产品其实并不擅长自学。
works.idea_en: Machine learning at home will need human teachers, and that teaching could become a job.
works.idea_zh: 家中的机器学习需要人类老师，而这种教学可能会成为一份工作。
works.method: Design fiction film with prop smart objects and training tools, made by Simone Rebaudengo with Yosuke Ushigome.
works.method_zh: 使用道具智能物件和训练工具拍摄的设计虚构短片，由 Simone Rebaudengo 与 Yosuke Ushigome 制作。

works.title: Believe it Yourself
works.description: 'Real-fictional' machine-learning kits trained on belief systems (Italian superstition, feng shui, astrology) that let amateurs build cameras which see the world through a chosen belief.
works.description_zh: 一套“真实—虚构”的机器学习套件，用信仰体系（意大利迷信、风水、占星）训练，让业余者自制能“透过某种信念”看世界的摄像头。
works.idea_en: A trained model is a belief system: it sees what its data taught it to see.
works.idea_zh: 一个训练好的模型就是一种信仰体系：它看到的，是数据教它看到的东西。
works.method: Modular hardware kits with cameras and pre-trained classifiers built from belief-based datasets, presented with manuals and posters.
works.method_zh: 带摄像头的模块化硬件套件，内置用信念数据集训练的分类器，配有说明书和海报。

works.title: UX Design Innovation: Challenges for Working with Machine Learning as a Design Material
works.description: A survey of UX practitioners showing that designers struggle to understand what machine learning can do and to prototype with it, and arguing that ML should be treated as a design material.
works.description_zh: 一项针对用户体验从业者的调查：设计师难以理解机器学习能做什么，也难以用它做原型；论文主张把机器学习当作一种设计材料。
works.idea_en: Designers need to handle ML like wood or code, sketching with its behaviours, not only receiving it from engineers.
works.idea_zh: 设计师需要像处理木材或代码一样处理机器学习，用它的行为来“画草图”，而不只是从工程师那里接手。
works.method: Survey of 51 UX designers plus analysis of design education and tools (Dove, Halskov, Forlizzi and Zimmerman, CHI 2017).
works.method_zh: 对 51 位用户体验设计师的调查，并分析设计教育与工具（Dove、Halskov、Forlizzi 与 Zimmerman，CHI 2017）。

paper.title: UX Design Innovation: Challenges for Working with Machine Learning as a Design Material

works.title: Re-examining Whether, Why, and How Human-AI Interaction Is Uniquely Difficult to Design
works.description: An analysis of why designing with AI is hard, tracing the difficulty to two sources: uncertainty about what a system can do and the complexity of its possible outputs.
works.description_zh: 一篇分析为什么与 AI 一起做设计特别困难的论文，把困难归结为两个来源：对系统能力的不确定，以及其可能输出的复杂性。
works.idea_en: AI is a design material whose behaviour cannot be fully sketched in advance; design methods have to account for that.
works.idea_zh: AI 是一种无法事先完整勾画其行为的设计材料，设计方法必须正视这一点。
works.method: Synthesis of prior research, the authors' design projects and teaching into a framework of four levels of AI design complexity (Yang, Steinfeld, Rosé and Zimmerman, CHI 2020).
works.method_zh: 综合既有研究、作者的设计项目与教学经验，提出 AI 设计复杂度的四层框架（Yang、Steinfeld、Rosé 与 Zimmerman，CHI 2020）。

paper.title: Re-examining Whether, Why, and How Human-AI Interaction Is Uniquely Difficult to Design

works.title: Thing Ethnography: Doing Design Research with Non-Humans
works.description: Cameras and sensors were attached to everyday objects (a kettle, a cup, a fridge) in homes so that designers could study daily life from the things' point of view.
works.description_zh: 研究者把摄像头和传感器装在家中的日常物件（水壶、杯子、冰箱）上，让设计师从“物”的视角研究日常生活。
works.idea_en: Things can be research partners: their sensor view reveals patterns of use that people do not notice or report.
works.idea_zh: 物可以成为研究伙伴：它们的传感器视角揭示出人们注意不到、也不会讲出来的使用模式。
works.method: Autographer cameras on household objects produced image streams analysed alongside interviews (Giaccardi, Cila, Speed and Caldwell, DIS 2016).
works.method_zh: 装在家居物件上的 Autographer 相机产生图像流，与访谈一起分析（Giaccardi、Cila、Speed 与 Caldwell，DIS 2016）。

paper.title: Thing Ethnography: Doing Design Research with Non-Humans

works.title: Products as Agents: Metaphors for Designing the Products of the IoT Age
works.description: Proposes three metaphors for smart products that act on their own: products as collectors of data, as actors that make decisions, and as creators that make new things with people.
works.description_zh: 为能够自行行动的智能产品提出三种隐喻：作为数据的“收集者”、作为做决定的“行动者”、作为与人共同创造的“创造者”。
works.idea_en: Once products have agency, designers need metaphors for the kind of relationship people will have with them.
works.idea_zh: 一旦产品拥有能动性，设计师就需要隐喻来描述人与它们之间将会是什么样的关系。
works.method: Design workshops and speculative product concepts analysed to derive the metaphors (Cila, Smit, Giaccardi and Kröse, CHI 2017).
works.method_zh: 通过设计工作坊和思辨产品概念的分析归纳出这些隐喻（Cila、Smit、Giaccardi 与 Kröse，CHI 2017）。

paper.title: Products as Agents: Metaphors for Designing the Products of the IoT Age

works.title: More-Than-Human Design and AI: In Conversation with Agents
works.description: Designers 'interviewed' conversational agents in homes as if they were research participants, treating them as others with their own perspective rather than as tools.
works.description_zh: 设计师在家庭环境中像访谈研究参与者一样“采访”对话式智能体，把它们当作有自身视角的他者而不是工具。
works.idea_en: Talking with an AI as a participant exposes its assumptions and makes more-than-human design concrete.
works.idea_zh: 把 AI 当作参与者来交谈，能暴露它的预设，也让“超越人类的设计”变得具体。
works.method: Design research with voice assistants, including interview scripts and designed artefacts, presented at DIS 2020 (Nicenboim, Giaccardi, Søndergaard, Reddy, Strengers, Pierce, Redström).
works.method_zh: 针对语音助手的设计研究，包括访谈脚本与设计物件，发表于 DIS 2020（Nicenboim、Giaccardi、Søndergaard、Reddy、Strengers、Pierce、Redström）。

paper.title: More-Than-Human Design and AI: In Conversation with Agents

works.title: Animistic Design
works.description: Proposes animism as a way to design smart objects: many small devices with their own personalities and agendas that negotiate with each other and with us, illustrated by van Allen's AniThings.
works.description_zh: 主张用“万物有灵”来设计智能物件：许多带有各自性格和意图的小设备，彼此之间以及与人之间相互协商；以 van Allen 的 AniThings 为例。
works.idea_en: Instead of one all-knowing assistant, design a society of partial, opinionated things whose uncertainty we can live with.
works.idea_zh: 与其做一个全知的助手，不如设计一个由偏执而局部的物组成的社会，让人能够与它们的不确定共处。
works.method: Theoretical argument drawing on philosophy and anthropology, with prototypes of networked objects with personalities (Marenko and van Allen, Digital Creativity 2016).
works.method_zh: 借助哲学与人类学的理论论证，配合具有性格的联网物件原型（Marenko 与 van Allen，《Digital Creativity》2016）。

paper.title: Animistic design: how to reimagine digital interaction between the human and the nonhuman

works.title: Re-Embodiment and Co-Embodiment
works.description: User enactments of social agents that move from one robot body to another (re-embodiment) or share one body among several agents (co-embodiment), asking how people track who they are talking to.
works.description_zh: 通过用户情境扮演，研究一个社交智能体从一个机器人身体转移到另一个身体（再具身），或多个智能体共享一个身体（共具身）时，人们如何判断自己在和“谁”说话。
works.idea_en: An AI's identity need not be tied to one body, which breaks our habit of reading a mind from a body.
works.idea_zh: AI 的身份不必绑定在一个身体上，这打破了我们从身体读取心智的习惯。
works.method: Speculative enactments in a mock service setting with robots and conversational agents (Luria, Reig, Tan, Steinfeld, Forlizzi and Zimmerman, DIS 2019).
works.method_zh: 在模拟服务场景中使用机器人与对话智能体进行思辨性情境扮演（Luria、Reig、Tan、Steinfeld、Forlizzi 与 Zimmerman，DIS 2019）。

paper.title: Re-Embodiment and Co-Embodiment: Exploration of Social Presence for Robots and Conversational Agents

works.title: Wekinator
works.description: Free software that lets musicians and artists train machine-learning models by example, demonstrating gestures and sounds, so that ML becomes an instrument-building material.
works.description_zh: 一款免费软件，让音乐人和艺术家通过示范手势与声音来训练机器学习模型，使机器学习成为制作乐器的材料。
works.idea_en: Interactive, example-based training puts people in the loop and makes ML something you play and sculpt rather than configure.
works.idea_zh: 交互式、基于示范的训练让人处在回路之中，把机器学习变成可以演奏和雕琢的东西，而不是需要配置的系统。
works.method: Supervised learning on user-recorded examples mapping any input (webcam, sensors, controllers) to any output over OSC, with rapid retraining.
works.method_zh: 对用户录制的示例进行监督学习，通过 OSC 把任意输入（摄像头、传感器、控制器）映射到任意输出，并可快速重新训练。

works.title: Teachable Machine
works.description: A web tool that lets anyone train an image, sound or pose classifier in the browser by showing a few examples to the webcam, with no code.
works.description_zh: 一个网页工具，任何人都可以对着摄像头示范几个例子，在浏览器里训练图像、声音或姿势分类器，无需写代码。
works.idea_en: Letting people train a model in a minute makes its dependence on examples, and its mistakes, directly felt.
works.idea_zh: 让人在一分钟内训练出一个模型，就能直接感受到它对示例的依赖以及它会犯的错。
works.method: Transfer learning on a pre-trained network runs locally in the browser with TensorFlow.js; version 2.0 (2019) added export of models.
works.method_zh: 在浏览器中用 TensorFlow.js 对预训练网络做迁移学习，全部在本地运行；2019 年的 2.0 版加入了模型导出。

works.title: Things We Could Design: For More Than Human-Centered Worlds
works.description: A book that argues design should move beyond human-centred design and treat things, including computational things, as participants with their own existence.
works.description_zh: 一本主张设计应超越“以人为中心”的书：把物（包括计算性的物）当作拥有自身存在的参与者。
works.idea_en: Designers can learn to design with and for things, not only for users.
works.idea_zh: 设计师可以学会与物一起设计、为物设计，而不仅仅为用户设计。
works.method: Posthumanist design theory drawing on Wakkary's research products (Morse Things, Tilting Bowl and others), published by MIT Press.
works.method_zh: 结合 Wakkary 的研究产品（Morse Things、Tilting Bowl 等）的后人类主义设计理论，由 MIT Press 出版。

paper.title: Things We Could Design: For More Than Human-Centered Worlds
